frame_75.jpg.note: Tiny rigid peg-like figures in neat rows, with identical poses and no contact shadows. They sit on a flat, untextured sand-coloured parade ground like a tabletop wargame diorama.

frame_20.jpg.note: Dense blocks of identical red specks lined up like game pieces, over flat low-poly sand and buildings. The figures have no individuality, no ground interaction and no believable scale.

frame_90.jpg.note: Smooth plastic-looking figures with waxy surfaces, stiff mannequin poses and cloned uniforms. They look pasted onto a photoreal street, and the street's grit and lighting don't carry over to them. Heads and faces are generic blobs, and the weak grounding makes them read as figurines.

frame_19.jpg.note: Same frame as frame_75: peg-like figures in rows on a flat sand plane, like a tabletop wargame board.

frame_66.jpg.note: Same frame as frame_20: identical red specks in blocks on flat sand, like game pieces.

frame_13.jpg.note: The people are better than in the other frames. Their sailor and soldier costumes are readable and their scale is plausible, and the crowd is varied enough to pass at a distance. Up close the figures are still smooth, matte and plasticky, with stiff poses and weak contact shadows, so they look like figurines in a photoreal set.
